- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5% above peak or align with 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment is positive but price history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of downward trend), model overestimates — apply downward bias of 2–5% to forecast.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often overestimates — apply 3–7% downward adjustment to avoid overconfidence.
- If forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., > 10% over 30d), check if sentiment was positive — if so, reduce forecast by 5–10% to reflect sentiment-driven overreaction.
- If forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., < -10%), sentiment was likely negative — increase forecast by 5–10% to account for sentiment reversal.
- For 30d horizon, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment shifts — use sentiment from last 5–7 days to adjust final 5–7 forecast points.
